in april, my dad suffered from a blood clot in his spine leaving him paralyzed from the chest down. my dad needed acute spinal rehabilitation after the hospital and deserved/ needed to be around people who really cared for him and his mental well-being. 

we were recommended kessler inpatient rehab for various reasons. this rehab is over an hour away for my family and i but due to past experiences at rehab facilities we needed my dad to get the best care possible. 

the first day my dad was admitted, an aid came in and insisted because he's obese and it would be too much work to constantly clean him so he needed an adult diaper. my dad was visibly upset and the aid made multiple remarks regarding his weight and how he was "too large" for her to do anything alone. my dad already felt like a burden, lost his meaning for life, and has had the hardest few years of his life. i have no tolerance for anyone bullying him but before i could say anything, one of the physical therapists, barbara, stepped into the room, heard what was being said and took care of the situation instantly. she filed a complaint with the head nurse and alerted her peers of what happened. she assured me no one, including my dad, deserves to be treated that way for any reason. 

after the first day, i felt like my dad was in good hands and the following months everyone at kessler would prove me right. 
i was fortunate enough to be able to visit my dad almost everyday but the days i or someone in my family couldn't visit, we felt safe knowing my dad was in good care. 

a special thank you to my dad's nurses and doctors, especially donna and alan. thank you to his physical therapists, barbara and tori, that kept us updated with his progress and worked with us to help him psychologically. 

after kessler, my dad had to go to a subacute rehab and we were happy he was closer to home but the staff and overall care was pathetic. my dad ended up in the hospital because of the lack of care and sadly he lost a lot of confidence, hope, and will to progress that the staff at kessler built. 

i wish my dad's insurance allowed him to stay at kessler longer. the disabled and their family deserve the level of care they provided.

i would recommend this specific kessler over and over and over again.

quick note: when i refer to adolescent(s), i am meaning ages 13-17, not children.)
my review on google 2 months ago was deleted. here it is copy and pasted, also edited a bit.
i was a patient at harbor oaks hospital many times in the adolescent (pediatric) section. your personal freedom here is pretty much deprived, as it is in most places. you have limited access to your clothes, hygiene material, books, anything used to help or regulate yourself. try to bring pg books, they won't be hesitant to take away any 'graphic' material (non-gut-churning material such as stephen king is not allowed, neither are books on psychology/mental health, or books with tragedy (drug addiction, mental health crisis, suicide, etc) as it is assumed other patients will read your materials. if lucky, the nurses/behavioral techs will take pity on your situation and let you have some of your 'graphic' books and the like. 
anyway, harbor oaks. not the best hospital. treatment is less than mediocre or adequate. no interacting with the opposite sex, which i can understand, although they don't stop children from butting into a situation such as phone calls, a personal matter with the nurses/behavioral techs, or whatever. children, if not enough beds on their side, will be housed on the teen girls' side. not the best choice. they will put transgenders on whichever side their sex at birth is. no lgbt rights whatsoever yet they won't stop patients from telling you graphic details of their sexual assault/abuse. being abused is a horrible thing and to be dealing with that, and have someone whom you've first met tell you their graphic details of abuse, is not something i enjoyed, and i wouldn't expect anyone to enjoy this either. the interaction with the same sex is not monitored. 
the food is not terrible, although what they promise for dinner is the opposite you receive. for example, if they promise cookies/cake/brownies, you may get gelatin or something of that sort. 
the social worker, eva, is inadequate and treats her adolescent patients like they are children. there are groups 2-4 times a day, and you will be frequently bored, no matter what they tell you. there is rarely treatment that addresses destructive behaviors or any other disorder besides clinical depression/persistent depressive disorder. if that is your issue, go to this hospital. if you struggle with something more complex, such as childhood abuse, destructive behaviors, eating disorders, personality disorders, etcetera, spend your money someplace else. 
they'll dope you up to as far as 600 m.g, morphing you into a zombie. you get no say in your aftercare or treatment in general. 
the average stay here, from what i remember, is 5-9 days. sometimes longer, sometimes shorter. the shortest i saw someone stay was 3-4 days, the longest, 13. it depends on your behavior and why you're there in the first place. 
the psychiatrist, dr. sanjeev venkataraman, (dr. raman, for short) can be pretty empty and fail to explain why you need a certain medication or give you an estimate for your discharge date. like most treatment facilities, more often than not, you will gain weight. the staff and psychiatrists will not care; you will be punished for not eating. 
your discharge date will likely be on a weekday. the psychiatrists rarely work on weekends. 
the groups range from rec. therapy (walking/exercising mindlessly in the adult gym for about an hour, making bracelets), and others. i cannot recall, as they were unimportant then and still unimportant now as i fail to remember them or their contents. 
the majority of adolescents were there for suicidal ideation. i wouldn't recommend sending your adolescent child here for substance abuse, as i recall, you are unable to mention anything related to addiction whatsoever. send them to a therapist. teen rehabs are disgusting and used for clout.
i don't know if harbor oaks made me worse in terms of suicidal ideation and destructive behaviors, though i know because of this facility and others, i've gained weight. this has sent my self-esteem to an all-time low. 
there have been reports of child abuse throughout this facility. i never saw or heard of anything like that whilst i was there multiple times. only after it'd been months after i left the most recent time i'd been there did i hear about a young child being slammed to the floor and getting a concussion. 
visitation times are, from what i recall, 3-5 times a week. phone calls twice a day, ten minutes. parents choose your contact list. only immediate family. 
as i mentioned you get no say in your aftercare and will likely be sent to a new oakland face to face location. this program, in particular, is pretty gross and please advocate for your rights. tell your parents not to send you. 
try to talk to your child before sending them away. sending them to a treatment facility such as harbor oaks may make them worse. do your research, don't believe everything you hear.

choose your hospital wisely:

i went to holy cross for a knee replacement.  the doctor was great and replacement doing good. however, when i came home i was on pain meds with tylenol.  doctors told me i most likely acquired a gram negative ecoli infection from the urinary catheter. the infection then grew into my blood and i became sepsis. after a week in another hospital and sent home with a mid line iv for antibiotics. i recovered after three weeks. i called holy cross hospital infectious department to let them know.  well i received no concern, no caring, and an excuse that i only had the catheter for one day. they also said, in order to pick up this infection in the hospital i would have had to have the catheter two days.  so not a very educated answer.  infections are acquired through direct contact and time exposure plays no role. 

copied from the internet:

causes
bacteria are normally found throughout the body including on the skin and in the intestines. when kept in balance, bacteria can help the body work normally. however, an imbalance of the bacteria or passing of bacteria to areas where there are no bacteria, can lead to an infection. an infection will develop if large amounts of bacteria are present, the bacteria are aggressive, or the immune system is weakened.

common ways for bacteria to pass to vulnerable parts of the body include:

use of medical devices that pass into the body, such as iv or urinary catheters
open wounds
contact with someone who has or has been exposed to gram-negative bacteria
risk factors
hospitalization is the most common risk factor for gram-negative bacterial infections. the longer the stay in the hospital, the higher the risk of infection.

other factors that increase the risk of a bacterial infection include:

recent surgery
use of urinary catheter
war wounds
dialysis for kidney disease , which includes regular use of iv lines or catheters
mechanical ventilator use
weakened immune system

with my experience it doesn't matter how good the doctor is.  if the hospital is a sick hospital, even the most mild surgery could cause sickness or even death. do your research.

i want to write a review on the inpatient dining "expressly for you." there is a menu that you can order what you want. there are specific times that you must be followed in ensure your meal order is placed in time. i have ordered many things from the menu, overall, i think they try to be to fancy and offer too many complex meal options. when i am sick, i prefer to eat very simple things without a ton of spice or flavor. this may just be me, but here are some of my thoughts on things i have ordered. 

scrambled eggs: the first time i ordered scrambled eggs they arrived with onions and peppers. this was not expected. the next time i ordered, i specified that i wanted scrambled eggs plain without onions or peppers. this time it arrived with a garnish orange slice that spread orange juice on my eggs and rendering them inedible. if you just want eggs, order without garnish! 

oatmeal: this is a solid basic. it is pretty bland by itself, but would highly recommend adding banana slices and a packet of cream cheese. 

pimento cheese plate: this is a generous scoop of pimento cheese and served with fresh veggies and pita. i wasn't feeling up to eating much, but what i did eat was great! 

cheeseburger and fries: one night i didn't get a dinner order placed, so they brought me a late tray option. it was a freshly made burger and fries. i may have just been super hungry, but this was amazing!! 

chicken salad sandwich: this was okay. the chicken salad had too much mayo for my taste, but not bad. 

chicken tenders: there was a lot of breading, but easy to peel off.

baked potato: good simple option and can order shredded cheese and sour cream on the side.

clear liquid diet: i'm not sure much can be done to make this better, but this is rough! the tray comes with broth (i sampled vegetable, chicken, and beef), jello, juice, or flavored water. the broth was always luke warm and never appealing, but this is likely a result of how i was feeling. pro tip:  the floors stock popsicles, so that is a great alternative/supplement to the tray. 

if you miss ordering off the menu or get to your room late the floors stock some boxed meals. one night my diet was advanced from clears to regular diet late and i wanted solid food. they brought me a turkey sandwich boxed lunch. i ate the turkey (not then bread) a standard basic turkey sandwich which is a good option when the cafeteria is closed. 

things i wish were on the menu: greek yogurt. they have sugary yogurt, but i really wish there was greek yogurt, low fat string cheese sticks, plain tuna without being in tuna salad, or other high protein simple options. 

the people that take your order on the phone are really helpful and willing to get you want you want!
